from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light enters media and seems to slow down.",
            "Refractive index n equals speed of light over velocity.",
            "n greater than one means light slows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The 'Slow-Motion' Illusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visuals
        surface = Line(start=self.grid["C1"], end=self.grid["C6"], color=BLUE)
        beam_in = Line(start=self.grid["A2"], end=self.grid["C4"], color=YELLOW)
        beam_out = Line(start=self.grid["C4"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=PURPLE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(surface))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(beam_in))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        eqn = MathTex(r"n = \frac{c}{v}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eqn, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(eqn))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.play(Create(beam_out))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Microscopic Origin: Induced Dipoles", [
            "Light waves oscillate electrons in atoms.",
            "Oscillating electrons re-radiate waves.",
            "Interference creates a slowed superposition."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        nucleus = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1)
        electron_orbit = Circle(radius=1.2, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
        electron = Dot(radius=0.15, color=ORANGE)
        
        atom = VGroup(nucleus, electron_orbit, electron)
        self.place_at_grid(atom, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animation
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.0), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(electron.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8000"))
        # Add a radiating wave representation
        wave = Circle(radius=0.1, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3)
        self.add(wave)
        wave.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.set_width(m.width + dt * 2))
        self.play(FadeIn(wave))
        self.wait(2)
        wave.remove_updater(wave.updaters[0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(FadeOut(wave))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Atoms have specific natural frequencies.",
            "Higher frequencies interact more strongly.",
            "Refractive index changes with wavelength.",
            "This phenomenon is called dispersion.",
            "Blue light oscillates tighter than red."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Dependence on Color: Dispersion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Visualization: Atoms/Molecules
        atoms = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid[pos]) for pos in ['B2', 'B4', 'C3', 'D2', 'D4']])
        self.play(Create(atoms))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        freq_wave = VGroup(*[
            Wave(freq=4).set_color(BLUE).scale(0.3).next_to(atoms[1], UP),
            Wave(freq=1).set_color(RED).scale(0.3).next_to(atoms[3], UP)
        ])
        self.play(Create(freq_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        # Graph of n(lambda)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        # Prism
        prism = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, UP*2, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(prism))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))
        # Final visualization
        self.wait(1)

class Wave(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, freq=1, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.set_points_smoothly([
            np.array([x, np.sin(freq * x * PI), 0]) for x in np.linspace(-1, 1, 50)
        ])

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Sellmeier equation describes material response.",
            "Refractive index depends on wavelength constants.",
            "Values peak near material absorption bands.",
            "Indices change rapidly near resonance.",
            "Prisms reveal this through color spreading."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Mathematics: The Sellmeier Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define equations
        sellmeier = MathTex(r"n^2(\lambda) = 1 + \sum_i \frac{B_i \lambda^2}{\lambda^2 - C_i}")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Sellmeier equation describes material response.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(sellmeier, 'C3')
        self.play(Write(sellmeier))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Refractive index depends on wavelength constants.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlight B_i, C_i
        terms = sellmeier.get_parts_by_tex("B_i")
        terms2 = sellmeier.get_parts_by_tex("C_i")
        self.play(Indicate(terms), Indicate(terms2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Values peak near material absorption bands.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        resonance_marker = Circle(color=RED, radius=0.3).move_to(sellmeier[0][16:20])
        self.play(Create(resonance_marker))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Indices change rapidly near resonance.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['D4'], end=self.grid['B4'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Prisms reveal this through color spreading.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        prism = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, UP*1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'E2')
        self.play(Create(prism))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refractive Index: Origins and Chromatic Dependence

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Slow-Motion' Illusion
sections.content: Hook the audience by illustrating light entering a medium. Briefly recall the definition: n = c/v. Establish that n > 1 implies light 'slows down' in materials. Prerequisite: Recall that light is an electromagnetic wave interacting with charged particles.
sections.example: A straw appears broken in a glass of water; we explain this as light 'bending' due to the medium's density.

sections.title: The Microscopic Origin: Induced Dipoles
sections.content: Explain that light's oscillating electric field drives electrons in atoms to oscillate. These oscillating electrons re-radiate waves that interfere with the incident wave, resulting in a phase-shifted (slowed) superposition. Use an animation showing an incident wave hitting an electron cloud.
sections.example: Think of a crowd of people (electrons) trying to pass a message; the 'dragging' effect caused by their interaction is what we perceive as a slower wave velocity.

sections.title: The Dependence on Color: Dispersion
sections.content: Introduce the concept of natural frequency (resonance) of atoms. Higher frequencies (blue light) interact more strongly than lower frequencies (red light). Display a graph showing the refractive index n(λ) vs. wavelength λ. Use a color-coded wave animation to show blue light oscillating 'tighter' against atomic structures.
sections.example: A chameleon's specialized skin cells; they change color by manipulating the refractive index and structural interference of light.

sections.title: Visualizing the Mathematics: The Sellmeier Equation
sections.content: Introduce the Sellmeier equation conceptually. Emphasize how n depends on λ based on material constants. Provide a graphical representation: a plot showing curves where n peaks near absorption bands. Connect this to the physical reality that near resonance, refractive index changes rapidly.
sections.example: Using a prism to split white light into a rainbow; the 'spread' of the colors is the direct physical manifestation of n varying by wavelength.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
sections.content: Synthesize the two main points: 1. Refraction is a collective response of electrons. 2. Chromatic dependence is due to varying resonance strengths. Summarize how this determines the design of optical instruments.
sections.example: Camera lenses: Designers must use 'Achromatic doublets' (two different glass types) to correct for the fact that blue and red light focus at different points due to dispersion.
